items.prompt: BST search/insert/delete cost is best stated as?
choices: O(h) where h is tree height
items.whyRight: Each step drops to one child; steps track height.
whyWrong: Constant time would require hashing or arrays by index.
Skewed trees make h = n, so log n is not guaranteed.

items.prompt: Without balancing, inserting sorted keys into a BST tends to produce?
items.whyRight: Each key goes right (or left), deepening one path.
whyWrong: Sorted inserts do not self-balance a plain BST.
Heap shape is a different structure.

items.prompt: Inorder successor of a node with a right child is?
choices: The leftmost node in the right subtree
The rightmost node in the left subtree
items.whyRight: Next larger key sits at the minimum of the right subtree.
whyWrong: Parent is only sometimes the successor (no right child case).
Rightmost left subtree is the predecessor pattern.
Successor still walks; threaded trees are optional.
Input order stability is not the BST balance claim.

items.prompt: Why might an interview prefer a hash set over a BST for “seen so far”?
choices: Expected O(1) vs O(log n) with no need for ordered iteration
Hash sets give sorted iteration free
whyWrong: BSTs store any ordered keys including ints.
Sorted iteration is the BST strength, not the hash set.
Memory depends on load and node overhead; not a universal win.

items.prompt: Deleting a BST node with two children commonly replaces it with?
choices: A random leaf from another tree
items.whyRight: Successor/predecessor preserve the search invariant with one splice.
